subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@acme.io>, Sam O'Neill <sam.oneill@acme.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 06 Jan 2027 18:02:00 +0000
Subject: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Hi Jane / Sam —

Thanks again for a great conversation today. Quick recap from our end to make sure we’re aligned before the technical deep-dive: 

Key pain points you highlighted:
- User-facing search latency spikes during peak traffic (~6–8pm PT) causing a 15–20% drop in conversion.
- High token cost for long-context prioritization workflows (product descriptions + user query).
- Limited ability to fail over gracefully between regions today.

Goals discussed:
1) 99th percentile latency target of <= 300ms for short prompts (<= 128 tokens) under baseline traffic.
2) Throughput to support 200 reqs/sec steady-state with bursts to 600 reqs/sec for short bursts.
3) Deployment topology that supports multi-region failover with cold-start < 60s and warm-line scaling.
4) Reduce per-token cost by ~30% via batching/quantization while preserving accuracy.

Technical requirements you mentioned:
- Preferred models: open-architecture LLMs you can host or compatible variants (we discussed 13B/70B footprints).
- KV caching for session-aware chat flows and prefix caching for product descriptions.
- Audit log retention for 90 days (SOC2-related).

Next steps we agreed:
- Schedule a technical deep-dive next week with your infra + ML engineer to walk through topology and run preliminary performance numbers.
- I’ll share our technical worksheet (model options, expected latency/throughput tradeoffs, quantization recommendations) and a short sample metrics CSV you can drop into the worksheet to get a first-pass estimate.
- Rishi to join the deep-dive for kernel/hardware recommendations; Neha to cover security/compliance items.

Proposed time for the deep-dive (please confirm): Thursday Jan 7, 10:00 AM PT / 6:00 PM UTC.

Attachments: redwood-technical-worksheet.pdf (worksheet), acme-metrics-sample.csv (sample traffic profile)

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Jane Park <jane.park@acme.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam O'Neill <sam.oneill@acme.io>
Date: Wed, 06 Jan 2027 19:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Marissa —

This is perfect, thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the goals on our side — 99th <= 300ms for short prompts and the throughput numbers are what we’re targeting.

Thursday Jan 7 at 10:00 AM PT works for Sam and me. We’ll also bring in our ML infra lead (Sam) and our SRE, Claire (CC’d on calendar invite). 

Two quick notes:
- We’ll share a recent traffic export (anonymized) ahead of the call — it’s about 72 hours of peak-week traffic.
- For models: our preference is to try a 13B variant first; if the latency looks good we can iterate to a 70B quantized profile.

See you tomorrow — sending over the export now.

Best,
Jane
Head of Product, Acme Commerce
jane.park@acme.io
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Park <jane.park@acme.io>, Sam O'Neill <sam.oneill@acme.io>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 07 Jan 2027 15:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive recap: latency/throughput SLOs and deployment topology

Thanks Jane — got the export, much appreciated.

Agenda for tomorrow’s deep-dive (30–45m):
1) Walk through the traffic sample and identify short/long prompt split.
2) Run through candidate model profiles (13B baseline, 13B int8 quantized, 70B int4 candidate).
3) Discuss serving topology: single-region warm pool + multi-region failover vs active-active routing.
4) Performance knobs: batching / prefix caching / KV cache hit expectations.
5) Next steps: a small pilot (2-week) to validate latency at scale.

I’ve attached the worksheet so your engineers can fill in environment details ahead of time. If you can drop the sample export into tab 'TrafficProfile' on the sheet that will help us produce rough QPS/latency estimates live.

Attachments: redwood-technical-worksheet.pdf, acme-metrics-sample.csv

Calendar invite: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=example-invite-id

See you then — Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jane Park <jane.park@acme.io>, Sam O'Neill <sam.oneill@acme.io>
Date: Thu, 07 Jan 2027 16:20:00 +0000
Subject: Internal: Post-call notes & action items (Acme Commerce deep-dive)

Rishi / Neha — quick internal summary after confirming the slot with Acme: 

What they want:
- 99th <= 300ms for short prompts, throughput ~200 rps baseline, bursts to 600 rps.
- Start with 13B model, iterate to a 70B candidate if latency budget allows.
- Multi-region failover; 90d audit log retention.

Immediate asks for the deep-dive:
- Rishi: please prepare kernel/hardware recommendations for both 13B and 70B quantized profiles (prefer GPU types + expected warm memory footprint + expected cold-start times). Bring any recent perf numbers for int8/int4 quantization that we can reference.
- Neha: prepare a 2-slide summary on audit logging, data retention options in Private vs Dedicated, and KMS integrations.

I’ll lead the call and walk through the worksheet. We should be able to provide rough latency/throughput estimates live if we have the traffic profile in the worksheet.

Follow-ups: after the call we’ll produce a short proposal with recommended topology and a pilot scope (2 weeks) including success criteria (p95/p99 targets, cost estimate delta).

Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
